text: Tern accepts a sensor sample only when its age is at most thirty seconds. An older sample is marked stale and never replaces the last accepted reading.
title: Tern freshness window

text: Gannet compares sensor timestamps with the gateway clock. A sample more than five seconds in the future is quarantined for a clock check.
title: Gannet clock checks

text: Ibis expects a heartbeat every ten seconds. Three missed heartbeats change the sensor status to unknown without inventing a zero reading.
title: Ibis heartbeat

text: Petrel restores fresh status after two consecutive timely samples. It keeps the stale interval in the audit record.
title: Petrel freshness recovery

text: Cairn binds every index to a corpus digest and document version. A changed document creates a new index identity before it can be searched.
title: Cairn revision binding

text: Slate rejects a replacement when the submitted previous version differs from the current version. The caller must read the current version before retrying.
title: Slate revision conflict

text: Flint snapshots are immutable. Corrections create a new snapshot and retain a link to the prior digest.
title: Flint immutable snapshots

text: Mica excludes withdrawn documents from the next published snapshot. Existing receipts retain the version they actually searched.
title: Mica withdrawal

text: Harbor permits at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes in a demo query. Byte length is checked before retrieval and whitespace-only queries are refused.
title: Harbor byte budget

text: Shoal permits twenty search operations per expiring demo session. An identical replay does not consume another operation.
title: Shoal session allowance

text: Reef retries one transient worker failure at most once. Each physical attempt has a separate identifier under the logical request.
title: Reef retry ceiling

text: Cove uses a five-second worker deadline. A timed-out client does not prove that worker execution stopped.
title: Cove deadline

text: Lumen records hashes for model and tokenizer files. A friendly model name alone cannot identify the bytes used for inference.
title: Lumen artifact binding

text: Prism refuses learned inference when a required model file is missing. It never silently substitutes lexical or hashing output.
title: Prism missing model

text: Halo checks vector dimension and finite values after encoding. Dense cosine similarity can be negative and is not a calibrated probability.
title: Halo vector checks

text: Beam uses the CPU execution provider and a fixed sequence limit. The provider, normalization and pooling policy belong in the model manifest.
title: Beam provider pin

text: Anchor reads an existing committed receipt after a lost response. It can return that result without invoking the encoder again.
title: Anchor committed replay

text: Keel returns a controlled transient error before the first encoding attempt. The second worker call gets a distinct attempt identity.
title: Keel transient failure

text: Rudder keeps request context isolated during concurrent work. A trace identifier is never a session credential.
title: Rudder context isolation

text: Moor commits business results even when its telemetry collector is offline. Missing spans remain unknown until independent observations arrive.
title: Moor collector outage

text: Archive expires demo receipts after one day. Retained study evidence contains synthetic digests and no session tokens.
title: Archive receipt retention

text: Vault binds accepted reports to hashes of raw observations. Altered raw bytes invalidate the rendered claim.
title: Vault evidence identity

text: Cache keys include the corpus digest and exact model bundle digest. A stale cache cannot be accepted under a new bundle identity.
title: Cache bundle key

text: Ledger retains failed and missing planned requests in its report. Successful files alone never define the study denominator.
title: Ledger rejected attempts
